reorder-point.context: A stock level line sloping down across a chart, crossing a dashed threshold where a small solid square marks the trigger. Used in inventory and purchasing tools for reorder levels and low stock alerts.

dead-stock.context: A box sitting on a shelf with a cobweb in the corner above it. Used for obsolete, unsold or slow moving inventory reports.

mailroom.context: A wall of small pigeonhole cubbies above a counter. Used for internal mail sorting, post rooms and parcel handling areas in offices.

packaging-hierarchy.context: A small box, a larger case and a tall pallet stack in a row of growing size. Used for packaging levels such as each, inner, case and pallet.

lead-time.context: A double-headed arrow spanning two vertical ticks with a parcel box above it. Used for order to delivery time and supply delay figures.

box-sizes.context: Three boxes of growing height standing in a row above a ruler line. Used for choosing carton sizes such as small, medium and large.

axle-load.context: A truck in side view with three arrows pressing down on its axles. Used for axle weight limits, overload checks and weighbridge results.

cotton-bale.context: A square bale with slightly bulging sides held by three horizontal wire bands. Used for cotton, wool, hay and other compressed fibre cargo.

steel-coil.context: A wide roll of steel sheet seen end on, wound in a spiral around a hollow core and resting on a cradle. Used for metal coil cargo and steel mill logistics.

serial-number-plate.context: A small metal plate with four rivets and a barcode strip between them. Used for equipment serial numbers, rating plates and asset tags.

freezer-bag.context: A flat plastic bag with a double zipper track across the top and a snowflake on its front. Used for frozen food storage and cold chain packing.

pillow-box.context: A small gift box with bowed top and bottom edges and two rounded ends that bulge like a pillow. Used for retail packaging of small items and favours.

spout-pouch.context: A standing flexible pouch with a screw cap spout fitted on its sloped top corner. Used for liquids, purees, refills and other spouted packaging.

labeling-parcel.context: A box with a shipping label stuck to its front and one corner peeling up. Used for label printing, label application and address labelling steps.

milk-run-logistics.context: A closed loop route with three square stops and a direction arrow. Used for scheduled collection rounds that pick up from several suppliers in one trip.

inventory-count-tag.context: A tall paper tag with a hole at the top, a number line and a perforated tear-off stub. Used for stocktake and physical inventory counting.

wrist-mounted-terminal.context: A small computer with barcode bars on its screen strapped across a forearm. Used for hands-free scanning and picking in warehouses.

radiation-portal-monitor.context: Two tall pillars either side of a lane with a radiation trefoil between them above a passing truck. Used for border and port checks for radioactive material.

strapping-machine.context: A table machine with an arch frame over a box and a strap band running around the box. Used for banding cartons and bundles at the end of a packing line.

coil-railcar.context: A flat railcar with two rounded hood covers, each shielding a round steel coil. Used for rail freight of steel and metal coils.

sideloader-forklift.context: A low flat truck with a tall mast at its side and round pipes stacked across its deck. Used for moving long loads such as pipes, timber and steel sections.

customs-carnet.context: A small booklet with a globe on its cover next to a stack of tear-out vouchers. Used for temporary import and export of goods without paying duty.

bulk-container.context: A shipping container with three round hatches on its roof and a discharge flap at one end. Used for loose cargo such as grain, powder and pellets.

letter-of-credit.context: A document showing a bank building with columns, a small ship below it and a signature line. Used for trade finance and payment guarantees between buyers and sellers.

un-packaging-symbol.context: A circle holding a lowercase u above a lowercase n. The mark for United Nations certified dangerous goods packaging, used on hazmat boxes and drums.

robotic-grid-storage.context: A top view of a square grid of storage cells with two small robots on the rails. Used for automated cube storage and grid based warehouse systems.

bullwhip-effect.context: A small box at the left with a wavy line running right whose swings grow larger and larger. Used to show how demand swings amplify up a supply chain.

pallet-pattern.context: A top view of a square pallet covered in rectangular boxes laid in an interlocking brick pattern. Used for palletising layouts and stacking plans.

converter-dolly.context: A small single-axle wheeled frame with a flat plate on top and a long sloping drawbar. Used for linking a second trailer behind a truck in a road train.

double-boxed-parcel.context: A small taped box standing inside a larger open box, with padding dots on both sides. Used for extra protective packing of fragile items.

cutout-foam-insert.context: A thick foam slab with a cavity cut in the shape of a camera body and lens. Used for custom case inserts that hold delicate equipment.

shelf-scanning-robot.context: A slim wheeled robot with a tall camera mast next to a store shelf, with scan lines reaching the products. Used for automated shelf audits and stock checking.

trailer-unloading-robot.context: A wheeled robot with a jointed arm reaching into the open back of a trailer to pull out a box. Used for automated truck and container unloading at docks.

pallet-shuttle.context: A rack lane in side view holding a pallet carried by a low flat shuttle on rails. Used for deep lane automated pallet storage.

art-shipping-crate.context: A wooden crate seen from above with foam blocks at each corner holding a framed painting. Used for museum and gallery art transport.

heavy-parcel.context: A taped box with a trapezoid weight block resting on top of it. Used for overweight parcel warnings and weight based shipping surcharges.

bulk-stockpile.context: An inclined conveyor belt dropping loose material onto the peak of a cone-shaped pile. Used for aggregate, coal, sand and grain stockyards.

tank-farm.context: Three squat round-topped storage tanks of different heights standing inside a low wall. Used for oil, fuel and chemical terminal storage.
